A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PyETR-based study despite the changed title. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and the four-page Appendix A, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on 383 generated reasoning problems, including model-level correlations, logical correctness and premise-order reversal results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds analyses relating fallacy rates to training-compute estimates and HELM capability scores.

M1.justification: The PyETR generation and inference procedures, response translation and logical correctness checking are retained. V2's monadic-predicate restriction and dataset-curation explanation are newly documented details; the PDFs do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 383 reasoning problems using the same four source templates, 12 thematic framings and premise-order intervention. V2 uses HELM scores and compute estimates as capability covariates, without adding administered reasoning tasks or domains.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster and all 38 model entries in the premise-reversal comparison remain unchanged. The new capability-proxy analyses reuse subsets of these models and introduce no new baseline method.

E3.justification: V2 adds correlation analyses using training-compute estimates for 19 models and mean HELM capability scores for nine models (Section 3.4). The original task evaluation, filtering, 2,400 thinking-token allowance and 3,000 output-token limit are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two robustness checks asking whether the fallacy-rate relationship survives alternative capability proxies: training compute and HELM scores. The existing premise-order intervention remains unchanged, and no additional ablation or error study appears.

E5.justification: Both retain Pearson and Spearman correlations, two-proportion z-tests, the same significance threshold and Figure 1's confidence bands. The new correlations extend existing statistical reporting; no seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports a training-compute Spearman correlation of rho = 0.489, p = 0.0334, and a HELM exponential-fit correlation of r = 0.796, p = 0.0103. Figure 1 and Tables 3–4 retain their original numerical results, including all premise-reversal entries.

T1.justification: Appendix A's 36 formal definitions and the main-text fallacy-rate equations are unchanged. The added remarks about first-order expressiveness and the monadic fragment explain the existing representation and experimental scope without developing new formal results.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a previously unobserved inverse-scaling phenomenon and convergence toward human cognition. V2 reframes the contribution as a setting-specific correlation in error composition and a theory-grounded evaluation pipeline, removing the separate advertised contribution of theoretical analysis about emerging human-like cognition.

C2.justification: V1 interprets the findings as evidence of emerging cognitive structures resembling human reasoning. V2 explicitly states that overlapping error patterns do not establish shared internal processes and restricts interpretation to this evaluation setting. It also identifies the monadic-predicate restriction; existing causality and training-trace caveats remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the monadic-predicate constraint and explains that 17 unsuitable items were excluded from 400 generated problems, yielding the already reported 383. It also supplies sources, subset sizes and access information for the HELM and training-compute analyses.

R1.justification: V2 adds Epoch AI and HELM references and removes McKenzie et al.'s Inverse Scaling citation and the associated discussion. The related-work survey and positioning against the earlier GPT-only ETR study otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introductory passages, theory overview and discussion are rewritten or condensed. The contribution list is recast, the inverse-scaling subsection is removed, and an AI-assistance disclosure is added. This substantially revises the narrative while preserving the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The same figure and four tables retain their display structures and content. Layout changes place Table 4 directly with the premise-reversal discussion instead of interrupting the conclusion, and bring Figure 1 and Table 3 onto the same page.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns its conclusions with the conditional error-composition evidence, especially by withdrawing inferences about shared internal cognition. Alternative capability-proxy checks and clearer curation details provide additional support and transparency. The gains remain limited: the new checks report only summary correlations for small subsets, and Section 5 retains the stronger assertion of a fundamental relationship rather than an artifact.
